output.brief: Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump came from the storage compaction tuning change pushed fleet-wide at about 23:40 on 2 Nov, not from gateway 5.8. Regional gateway arrival times were staggered over six hours. Latency jumped in every cell within minutes of the config push, and the cells that hadn't yet received 5.8 jumped too. One cell, aps-3, got 5.8 but skipped the config push, and its latency stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. After the push, compaction threads went from 2 to 6, disk use went to 97%, and disk read waits rose from 9 to 205 ms. A fleet-wide rollback would remove the security fix, which is due by 30 Nov, and wouldn't fix latency. Network and traffic growth don't explain the timing. Next step: revert the compaction change in one cell first, e.g. use-1. Watch p99 and compaction backlog, then extend the revert. Don't pause compaction, because backlog would reach the 15% danger point. Hold off on throttling Orrin until the backlog attribution report due 10 Nov. Confidence is high. The main unknown is what drove the backlog growth.
